paper.title: SPARKLE: A Nonparametric Approach for Online Decision-Making with High-Dimensional Covariates

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandit with high-dimensional covariates and sparse additive RKHS rewards
unmapped: Each arm's reward function is sparse additive: sum of at most s_0 univariate components, each in a Sobolev-type RKHS of smoothness m (kernel Fourier transform ~ (1+w^2)^{-m}, m>3/2)
Covariates in [0,1]^d with density bounded above and below
Compatibility condition on the additive function class
Regularity of nearly-optimal regions and decision boundaries (Assumptions 5-6)
Each arm optimal on a region of probability at least p*
Tsybakov-type margin condition with exponent alpha in [0,1]
The learner knows the RKHS smoothness m and the kernel
settings.definition_quote: At each time $t = 1, \ldots, T$, a decision-maker observes a $d$-dimensional covariate vector $\bx_t$ which is generated independently from a fixed but unknown distribution with support $\Omega\subset \RR^d$, then selects an arm $\pi_t \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$ to pull, and receives a random reward $y_t \in \RR$. ... $f_k^*(\bx) = \sum_{j=1}^{d} f^*_{k,(j)}(x_{(j)})$

settings.name_in_paper: RKHS contextual bandit with sparse additive rewards (lower bound)
unmapped: Sparse additive RKHS rewards of smoothness m (Sobolev-type kernel)
Assumptions 1-8 of the paper (density, compatibility, region regularity, optimal-region mass, margin condition with exponent alpha)
settings.definition_quote: For any non-anticipating policy $\pi$, there exists a contextual bandit instance with horizon $T$ that satisfies Assumptions \ref{assum_densitybound}--\ref{assum_margin}

settings.name_in_paper: RKHS contextual bandit with general (non-additive) d-dimensional RKHS rewards (lower bound)
unmapped: Reward functions in a d-dimensional RKHS of smoothness m with stationary kernel (Fourier transform ~ (1+||w||^2)^{-m}), no additivity
Modified assumptions 3',5',6',8' with critical scale T^{-(2m-d)/(4m)}; margin condition with exponent alpha
settings.definition_quote: For each $k=1,\ldots,K$, the reward function $f_k^* \in \cN_{\Phi^{\prime}}(\Omega)$, where $\Phi^{\prime}:\Omega\times \Omega\mapsto \RR$ is a positive definite kernel

symbols.m_rkhs: RKHS (Sobolev) smoothness parameter m > 3/2 of the univariate kernel

conditions: Assumptions 1-8: covariates i.i.d. with density in [p_min, p_max] on Omega in [0,1]^d
sparse additive rewards with at most s_0 nonzero components, each in RKHS with Fourier decay (1+w^2)^{-m}, m > 3/2
nearly-optimal regions regular (Assumption 5) and decision boundary regularity (Assumption 6)
each arm optimal on a region with probability >= p* > 0
margin condition with exponent alpha in [0,1]: P(0<|f_i-f_j|<=delta) <= C_0 delta^alpha for delta >= delta_0
tuning: epoch lengths tau_q = ceil(C_1 (s_0^{(2m+1)/(4m)} 2^{q+4})^{(4m+2)/(2m-1)} log(dT) log(T))
regularization (rho, lambda) per Theorem 1 with delta = 1/T

source.label: thm:regretupperbound
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions \ref{assum_densitybound}--\ref{assum_margin} hold. Then, the expected cumulative regret of SPARKLE satisfies \begin{align*} R_T=\tilde O\left(s_0^{1 + \frac{6m+1}{2m(2m-1)}}T^{1-\frac{(2m-1)(1+\alpha)}{4m+2}}\log(d)\right). \end{align*}

results.notes: Regret defined via expected reward functions against per-context oracle, so pseudo-regret. s_0 is a known upper bound on sparsity (mapped to s_sparse). Tilde hides log T factors. Polynomial compute: SOCP solved O(log T) times. Proof ending states a slightly different s_0 exponent; recorded theorem statement.

conditions: hard instance: K=2, s_0=1, Gaussian noise with variance in (8/9,1), uniform covariates

source.label: thm_lb
source.quote: Fix $\alpha>0$ and $m>0$ with $\alpha m\le 1$. For any non-anticipating policy $\pi$, there exists a contextual bandit instance with horizon $T$ that satisfies Assumptions \ref{assum_densitybound}--\ref{assum_margin} such that, for some constant $C>0$ depending only on the instance class (not on $\pi$), \begin{align*} R_T(\pi) \geq C T^{1-\frac{m(1+\alpha)}{2m+1}}. \end{align*}

results.notes: Gap to upper bound is O~(T^{(1+alpha)/(4m+2)}).

conditions: hard instance: K=2, Gaussian noise, uniform covariates on [0,1]^d

source.label: thm_lb_withd
source.quote: Fix $\alpha>0$ and $m>0$ with $\alpha m\le d$. For any non-anticipating policy $\pi$, there exists a contextual bandit instance with horizon $T$ that satisfies Assumptions ... such that, for some constant $C>0$ depending only on the instance class (not on $\pi$), \begin{align*} R_T(\pi) \geq C T^{1-\frac{m(1+\alpha)}{2m+d}}. \end{align*}

results.notes: Shows curse of dimensionality without additivity. Hard instances also lie in Hölder class, giving a Hölder lower bound as byproduct. Theorem thm:lbwithoutregularity (regret/upper-bound ratio -> infinity without Assumptions 5-6) not recorded since it gives no explicit bound expression.
